cardiovascular.name: Cardiovascular system
cardiovascular.role: Your heart and blood vessels move oxygen and nutrients around the body. In microgravity, fluids shift towards your head and the heart works less hard.
recommendations: Drink at least 2 litres of water per day.

respiratory.name: Respiratory system
respiratory.role: Your lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide. Cabin atmosphere and dust can affect how comfortably you breathe.
recommendations: Report any persistent cough or irritation.
Wear a mask during filter maintenance.

brain.name: Brain and cognition
brain.role: Your brain manages attention, memory and coordination. Sleep, workload and radiation exposure can influence cognitive performance.
recommendations: Take short breaks during long procedures.

eyes.name: Eyes and vision
eyes.role: Your eyes can change shape slightly during long missions as fluid shifts upward. Regular checks catch changes early.

skeletal.name: Skeletal system
skeletal.role: Your bones support your body and store calcium. Without gravity loading, bones lose density unless you exercise.
recommendations: Take your vitamin D portion with meals as planned.

muscular.name: Muscular system
muscular.role: Your muscles keep you strong for EVA and landing. Weight-bearing muscles weaken quickly in microgravity.

immune.name: Immune system
immune.role: Your immune system protects against infection. Stress, radiation and sleep loss can lower its response in space.

metabolism.name: Metabolism and nutrition
metabolism.role: Metabolism turns food into energy. Onboard diet, exercise and stress can change your glucose.
recommendations: Measure fasting glucose when the protocol asks for it.

heartRate.name: Resting heart rate
heartRate.description: Beats per minute while fully at rest. Fluid shifts in microgravity can change your resting rate.

bloodPressure.name: Blood pressure
bloodPressure.description: Systolic and diastolic pressure in your arteries. Tracks how your heart and vessels adapt to weightlessness.

spo2.name: Blood oxygen saturation
spo2.description: Percentage of oxygen carried by your red blood cells. Reflects cabin atmosphere and lung function.

respRate.name: Respiratory rate
respRate.description: Breaths per minute at rest, measured by the chest strap sensor.

reactionTime.name: Psychomotor reaction time
reactionTime.description: Mean response time on the 3-minute vigilance task. Sensitive to fatigue, sleep loss and workload.

eyePressure.name: Intraocular pressure
eyePressure.description: Fluid pressure inside the eye. Monitored for changes associated with long-duration spaceflight.

urinaryCalcium.name: Urinary calcium
urinaryCalcium.description: Calcium leaving the body over 24 hours. An indirect marker of bone loss in microgravity.

gripStrength.name: Grip strength
gripStrength.description: Maximum hand strength. Reflects muscle loss during the mission.

bodyTemperature.name: Body temperature
bodyTemperature.description: Core body temperature. Can signal an infection or an immune response.

glucose.name: Blood glucose
glucose.description: Blood sugar. Diet, exercise and in-flight stress can change it.

sleepHours.name: Sleep hours
sleepHours.description: Hours slept (wristband or manual). Onboard light and schedules disrupt sleep.

radDoseDaily.name: Daily radiation dose
radDoseDaily.description: Dosimeter dose for the day. It rises during solar events.

radDoseCum.name: Cumulative radiation dose
radDoseCum.description: Career cumulative dose, compared with NASA limits.

bodyMass.name: Body mass
bodyMass.description: Weight measured on board. Microgravity can reduce muscle and bone.

tests.subtitle: Keep your mind active and catch changes early

tests.keepGoing: A few minutes a day is enough: what matters is comparing with yourself.
tests.disclaimer: Training and self-tracking exercises, not medical assessments. Inspired by NASA's Cognition battery.

reaction.title: Alertness reflexes
reaction.why: Fatigue, sleep loss and radiation can slow your reactions. This PVT-style test spots it by comparing you with yourself.
steps: Wait with your finger ready over the screen.
When the panel turns green, tap it as fast as you can.
Tapping too early counts as a false start.

vision.title: Visual clarity
vision.why: Vision can change on long flights (SANS, spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome). Catching changes early helps.
steps: Hold the phone about 40 cm away, in good light.
Cover one eye at a time.
Show which way the legs of the E point. Each correct answer makes it smaller.

stroop.title: Mental agility
stroop.why: Measures attention and control: deciding fast while ignoring distracting information.
steps: A color name appears painted in another color.
Tap the INK COLOR, not what the word says.
There are 20 words: be fast but accurate.

memory.title: Spatial memory
memory.why: Trains working memory, key to following complex procedures on board.
steps: Watch which squares light up and in what order.
Repeat the sequence by tapping them.
Each success adds a square; two misses in a row end the test.

vision.distance: Hold the phone about 40 cm from your face.
vision.question: Which way do the legs of the E point?
vision.asymmetry: There is a difference between your eyes. Log it and check the Eyes system; if it persists, tell your crew.
